scenes.tts: Spots of light drive the retina well. In cat visual cortex, the same spots often did little. A bar at the right angle drove some cells hard. Why would a bar win?
scenes.visual: A grey screen. A small white spot appears; beside it a spike raster ticks only rarely. The spot is replaced by a tilted white bar and the raster runs densely. On-screen text: Why would a bar beat a spot?
scenes.narration: Spots of light drive the retina well. In cat visual cortex, the same spots often did little. A bar at the right angle drove some cells hard. Why would a bar win?

scenes.tts: Start in the retina. Every visual neuron watches one patch of the world, its receptive field.
scenes.visual: The view zooms in on a simple eye, its retina and one ganglion cell. A round patch is drawn on the grey screen and linked by a thin line to the ganglion cell. Label: receptive field.
scenes.narration: Start in the retina. Every visual neuron watches one patch of the world, its receptive field.

scenes.tts: Take an on-centre ganglion cell. Light on its small round centre excites it. Light on the ring around it, the surround, inhibits it.
scenes.caption: Take an ON-centre ganglion cell. Light on its small round centre excites it. Light on the ring around it, the surround, inhibits it.
scenes.visual: The patch fills in: a green centre marked + and a magenta ring marked −. Labels: centre (ON), surround (OFF). A vertical sum meter appears beside the patch, empty, with a zero line and the label: stimulus drive (zero = steady background). No threshold line is drawn on it. A spike raster below ticks slowly: label, spontaneous firing.
scenes.narration: Take an ON-centre ganglion cell. Light on its small round centre excites it. Light on the ring around it, the surround, inhibits it.

scenes.tts: Shine a small spot that just fills the centre. It lands only on plus, so the cell fires faster.
scenes.visual: A small white spot slides onto the green centre. The meter rises green above zero; the raster speeds up well above its slow spontaneous ticks.
scenes.narration: Shine a small spot that just fills the centre. It lands only on plus, so the cell fires faster.

scenes.tts: Now light the whole patch, centre and ring together. What will the cell do?
scenes.visual: The spot fades. On-screen text: Light over the whole patch?
scenes.narration: Now light the whole patch, centre and ring together. What will the cell do?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Very little. The centre adds plus, the ring adds minus, and the two largely cancel.
scenes.visual: Diffuse light washes over the whole patch. Green and magenta arrows push the meter in opposite directions; it barely moves from zero. The raster stays near its slow spontaneous rate.
scenes.narration: Very little. The centre adds plus, the ring adds minus, and the two largely cancel.

scenes.tts: Light the ring alone, and the sum goes negative, so firing drops below its spontaneous rate.
scenes.visual: A white ring lights only the magenta surround. The meter drops into magenta below zero and the raster slows almost to nothing.
scenes.narration: Light the ring alone, and the sum goes negative, so firing drops below its spontaneous rate.

scenes.tts: When that light goes off, the cell gives a brief burst. That burst answers a change in light, which the sum alone does not capture.
scenes.visual: The ring goes dark. The raster shows a brief burst, then returns to its slow spontaneous ticks. The burst is tagged: response to light going off, not part of the sum. The meter returns to zero.
scenes.narration: When that light goes off, the cell gives a brief burst. That burst answers a change in light, which the sum alone does not capture.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule for cells like this one. Add up the light in the field. Light on an on region counts as plus. Light on an off region counts as minus.
scenes.caption: So here is the rule for cells like this one. Add up the light in the field. Light on an ON region counts as plus. Light on an OFF region counts as minus.
scenes.visual: A caption card builds line by line: Approximate rule. Add up the light. ON region: plus. OFF region: minus.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule for cells like this one. Add up the light in the field. Light on an ON region counts as plus. Light on an OFF region counts as minus.

scenes.tts: A bigger sum means stronger drive. A sum near zero leaves the spontaneous rate. A positive sum can raise firing, and a negative sum lowers it, down to zero.
scenes.visual: The card adds: Bigger sum, stronger drive. Near zero: spontaneous rate. Positive: can raise firing. Negative: lower, down to zero.
scenes.narration: A bigger sum means stronger drive. A sum near zero leaves the spontaneous rate. A positive sum can raise firing, and a negative sum lowers it, down to zero.

scenes.visual: The full rule card holds on screen: Approximate rule. Add up the light: plus on ON, minus on OFF. Bigger sum, stronger drive; firing also depends on baseline, threshold and saturation.

scenes.tts: Where the patch sits tells you which part of the world the cell reports.
scenes.visual: The card shrinks to a corner. A visual field appears with several patches scattered across it, each linked to its own cell. Label: where.
scenes.narration: Where the patch sits tells you which part of the world the cell reports.

scenes.tts: How plus and minus are laid out tells you which stimulus it reports best.
scenes.visual: One patch enlarges: its green and magenta regions rearrange into different layouts, a ring and then strips. Label: what.
scenes.narration: How plus and minus are laid out tells you which stimulus it reports best.

scenes.tts: Cells of the thalamic relay, the lateral geniculate nucleus, have fields of the same kind.
scenes.caption: Cells of the thalamic relay, the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN), have fields of the same kind.
scenes.visual: A row of round centre-surround fields labelled LGN, each green centre with a magenta ring. An arrow points onward to a block labelled V1, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Cells of the thalamic relay, the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN), have fields of the same kind.

scenes.tts: It is a good first approximation for many cells in the retina and thalamus, and for simple cells in cortex. Later we find where it stops.
scenes.visual: Three labelled icons light up in a row: retina, LGN, V1 simple cell, under the heading: good first approximation. A fourth icon, complex cell, stays greyed out with a small flag: beyond one sum.
scenes.narration: It is a good first approximation for many cells in the retina and thalamus, and for simple cells in cortex. Later we find where it stops.

scenes.tts: Keep the rule. Add up the light in the patch, plus on on regions and minus on off regions.
scenes.caption: Keep the rule. Add up the light in the patch, plus on ON regions and minus on OFF regions.
scenes.visual: The rule card returns to full screen.
scenes.narration: Keep the rule. Add up the light in the patch, plus on ON regions and minus on OFF regions.
